text: Rust treats a mutable reference as unique, so the compiler can assume nothing else reads or writes that value while it exists. Allowing two at once would permit aliased mutation, the class of bugs behind data races and single-threaded errors such as iterator invalidation.
thought:
Rust forbids two mutable references to the same value to prevent data races. This prevents the bug class of concurrent modification.

The rule also prevents aliasing and mutation bugs like iterator invalidation and use-after-free.

The compiler assumes mutable references are unique. Aliased mutable access violates that assumption and causes memory corruption.
